security_audit.summary: The static findings are almost entirely false positives from Markdown examples, WordPress documentation, placeholders, and benign template identifiers. I found no prompt-injection text or hidden execution path, but the REST endpoint template has real validation and authorization gaps around status and metadata updates.

remediation.issue: Editable REST route accepts status changes without declared validation.
remediation.suggestion: Add status to the route args with sanitize and validate callbacks, and require publish_posts before allowing publish transitions.

remediation.issue: REST callbacks save custom metadata directly from request parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Declare price, location, and featured arguments with validation and sanitization before calling update_post_meta.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples use absolute skill paths and operational cron commands that trigger static scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Use portable relative paths in examples and clearly label cron snippets as manual operational guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated REST Status Update
semantic_findings.description: The editable REST route declares title and content arguments, but the update callback also accepts a status request parameter and writes it to post_status. The permission callback only checks edit_post, so publishing transitions may lack explicit publish_posts validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The route args omit status while the callback reads and writes it directly. WordPress permissions may mitigate some cases, but the template should validate status and check publishing capability explicitly.

semantic_findings.title: Unsanitized REST Metadata Writes
semantic_findings.description: The create and update callbacks save price, location, and featured metadata directly from request parameters. The route does not define validation or sanitization for those fields before update_post_meta.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The request values are passed directly into update_post_meta in both create and update paths. This is a clear template-level validation gap, even if later output may escape values.

content.user_title: Build Secure WordPress Themes and Plugins
content.value_statement: WordPress projects often need secure, standards-based PHP patterns. This skill provides practical guidance, templates, and review prompts for theme and plugin development.
actual_capabilities: Explains WordPress PHP, JavaScript, and CSS coding standards.
Provides starter templates for custom post types, taxonomies, meta boxes, REST endpoints, and plugin skeletons.
Guides reviews for sanitization, escaping, nonces, capability checks, and prepared SQL statements.
Covers performance patterns for queries, caching, asset loading, images, and cron behavior.
Includes a scaffold script for generating boilerplate WordPress code.
Documents common hooks, filters, template hierarchy, and recommended development patterns.
limitations: Generated templates still require project-specific review before production use.
The skill does not test code against a live WordPress installation.
Plugin recommendations may need current version, license, and compatibility checks.
Security guidance does not replace a full application security review.

use_cases.title: Create Plugin Boilerplate
use_cases.description: Generate a starter structure for a custom post type, taxonomy, meta box, or REST endpoint.

use_cases.title: Review Theme Security
use_cases.description: Check form handlers, AJAX actions, REST callbacks, and template output for common WordPress security mistakes.

use_cases.title: Improve Site Performance
use_cases.description: Identify better query limits, caching options, image handling, and asset-loading patterns for a WordPress build.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Plugin File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WordPress plugin file. Check sanitization, escaping, nonces, and capability checks. Return prioritized fixes with file references.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Custom Post Type
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WordPress custom post type for my project. Include labels, rewrite settings, REST support, and security notes for admin output.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WP_Query usage. Suggest safer limits, cache strategy, pagination behavior, and any better taxonomy or meta-query design.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure REST Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a WordPress REST endpoint for authenticated content updates. Include permission callbacks, argument validation, sanitization, and response behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a form handler that saves post metadata.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing nonce checks, weak capability checks, unsanitized fields, and unsafe output. It proposes WordPress API replacements.

output_examples.input: Create a Property custom post type with a featured flag.
output_examples.output: The result outlines the post type settings, admin columns, labels, REST support, and security checks needed before deployment.

output_examples.input: Audit a theme for performance issues.
output_examples.output: The response highlights expensive queries, missing cache layers, heavy asset loading, image opportunities, and safer cron scheduling choices.

best_practices: Review every generated template for project-specific permissions and data flow.
Add sanitization, escaping, nonce checks, and capability checks before deployment.
Verify plugin and external dependency choices against the current production environment.
anti_patterns: Copying scaffolded code directly into production without review.
Using public REST routes for private or mutable content.
Hard-coding credentials, domains, or filesystem paths in reusable WordPress code.

faq.question: Does this skill run WordPress commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and scaffold commands that a user or agent may choose to run.

faq.question: Can it create custom post types?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance and templates for custom post types, taxonomies, meta boxes, and admin columns.

faq.question: Can it review WordPress security?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on sanitization, escaping, nonces, capabilities, SQL safety, uploads, AJAX, and REST routes.

faq.question: Are the templates production ready?
faq.answer: They are starter templates. Developers should adapt names, permissions, data validation, and project rules before deployment.

faq.question: Does it help with performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers query limits, transients, object cache, asset loading, images, cron, and monitoring practices.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
